::: {.cite-bar .domain-defense-arms}
[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Pub. L. 115-232]{.cite} [132 Stat. 1636]{.cite} [50 U.S.C. 4565]{.cite}
:::

Expanded the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States, which reviews foreign acquisitions for national security risk. Coverage now extends beyond takeovers to minority stakes in sensitive businesses and to some real estate.

## Key provisions

- Jurisdiction over non-controlling investments in businesses dealing with critical technology, critical infrastructure, or sensitive personal data.
- Jurisdiction over real estate transactions near military and other sensitive sites.
- Mandatory filings for certain transactions, including those with foreign government involvement.
- Filing fees, longer review timelines, and more resources for the committee.

## Why it matters

The committee dates to a 1975 executive order and the 1988 Exon-Florio amendment. This act rewrote Section 721 of the [Defense Production Act](dpa-1950.qmd) and was enacted with the [Export Control Reform Act](ecra-2018.qmd) in the same title of [the FY2019 NDAA](ndaa-annual.qmd).

## Current status

In force.
